_comment: T-RESUME-PHONE-RESTART-DESYNC (RESUME-PROTOCOL RULE 30). ONE vector file, TWO halves of one cross-surface assumption: the RELAY decides whether a re-joining phone may be resumed (lib/resumeGate-core.js), and the WEB decides what to do with a resume it is handed (hooks/phoneE2e.ts resumedPeerSessionVerdict / pairEndedErrorForReason). Consumed by tests/e2e-resume-phone-restart-contract.test.mjs. Rows are named; every row says WHY it exists. Edit rows HERE only.
_incident: live-acceptance-vc67-20260925T0100Z, 23:27-23:50Z, prod 4dc9282, phone v67. Verified pair (SAS matched) -> phone app force-stopped and restarted -> relay auto-resumed (droppedRole=phone, gap=13ms) -> web kept its E2E session, phone came back with none, inbound plaintext SMS_RECEIVED never rendered, phone's LEAVE_ACTIVE was 'from non-active phone - ignored', pair wedged for the full 180 s hold.

relayRows.name: browser-dropped-resumes
relayRows.why: The unchanged path, and the reason this gate is keyed on whether the PHONE returned rather than on the claim's droppedRole. A browser reload or panel close is the COMMON resume and the phone never left room.active, so its session is by construction still the pair's. A fix that broke this would turn every side-panel close into a re-pair.

relayRows.name: phone-dropped-session-intact-same-kid-resumes
relayRows.why: A genuine blip: doze, Wi-Fi/cell handoff, the java-websocket 15 s ping timeout. The process lived, so e2eSession lived, and the phone names the pair's kid. This MUST still resume or the fix costs every user a re-pair on every cellular hiccup - a worse product than the bug.

relayRows.name: phone-dropped-session-absent-terminates
relayRows.why: THE PROD ROW. Force-stop -> fresh process -> e2eSession is null -> the phone declares session=0 and rejoins within milliseconds. Resuming here re-sends sealed key material to a peer that cannot open it and leaves the web sealed-expecting over a plaintext phone.

relayRows.name: phone-dropped-different-kid-terminates
relayRows.why: The phone holds A session, just not THIS one - it re-paired elsewhere, or a second handset on the same account answered. Byte-identical block, different SK: the same desync as the absent row, reached by a path a presence boolean alone would have waved through. This is why the declaration carries the kid and not a bit.

relayRows.name: phone-dropped-undeclared-terminates
relayRows.why: An APK that predates ?session= (every build up to and including vc67). Silence is not evidence of a session, and treating it as one reproduces the incident exactly. Deploy-ordering consequence stated in the resume: until vc68 ships, a SEALED pair whose phone blips re-pairs instead of resuming. Plaintext pairs are untouched (see the row below).

relayRows.name: phone-dropped-plaintext-pair-resumes
relayRows.why: No e2e block is stashed, so there is no session to have lost and nothing the resume can desync. Without this row the gate would break resume for every plaintext pair on every older APK - a regression far wider than the bug, affecting users who never turned Encrypted mode on.

leaveActiveRows.name: leave-active-from-the-active-phone-honoured
leaveActiveRows.why: The ordinary Disconnect on a fully live pair. Unchanged behaviour, pinned so the hold fix cannot be mistaken for the whole rule.

leaveActiveRows.name: leave-active-during-survivor-hold-honoured
leaveActiveRows.why: THE PROD ROW. During a hold the phone is NOT room.active.phone - it is the side that dropped - so the strict identity test answered 'LEAVE_ACTIVE from non-active phone - ignored' and the user's own Disconnect did nothing for 180 s.

leaveActiveRows.name: leave-active-during-a-browser-dropped-hold-ignored
leaveActiveRows.why: The held pair's phone is the SURVIVOR here, so it IS room.active.phone and takes the first row. A phone reaching this branch under a browser-dropped claim is some OTHER handset in the same room, and it may not end a pair it is not in.

leaveActiveRows.name: leave-active-with-no-pair-and-no-claim-ignored
leaveActiveRows.why: The branch's ORIGINAL job, kept intact: a lobby phone that was never part of an active pair cannot tear one down. Widening the honour rule until this row flipped would hand any second device on the account a remote Disconnect.

leaveActiveRows.name: leave-active-with-an-expired-claim-ignored
leaveActiveRows.why: A claim past its expiry is not a hold. Reading room.resumable without checking expiresAt would honour a Disconnect against a pair the janitor has already released.

webRows.name: web-resumed-kid-matches-ok
webRows.why: The blip a user must never be made to re-pair for. The relay resumed, the phone named our kid, nothing happens.

webRows.name: web-resumed-kid-mismatch-lost
webRows.why: The page's own re-verification, independent of the relay's verdict. A page that trusted the relay and held no fact of its own would have delegated its session lifetime to the relay - the same mistake A3 refuses for userId.

webRows.name: web-resumed-peer-declares-no-session-lost
webRows.why: The prod shape as the page would see it if the relay ever forwarded it: the phone says it holds nothing. Keeping decrypt-expecting state here is what silently swallowed the inbound SMS.

webRows.name: web-resumed-no-peer-session-field-ok
webRows.why: NOT CHECKABLE, and the expensive mistake here is the false positive. An older relay, or a resume where the phone SURVIVED and its join-time declaration would be stale, both arrive with no field. Tearing down a healthy verified pair on an absent field would be a self-inflicted outage.

webRows.name: web-fresh-pairing-never-checked
webRows.why: A fresh Accept re-derives everything on both sides, so there is no continuity claim to verify. Running the check here would refuse first pairings whenever a stale kid was still in the ref.

webRows.name: web-resumed-while-we-hold-no-session-ok
webRows.why: A plaintext pair resuming. We hold no kid, so we cannot be out of step with anybody, and there is no sealed state to tear down.

webRows.name: web-resumed-malformed-peer-session-ok
webRows.why: The field is a relay-chosen value and its shape is proven at the read, not assumed. A truthy string where a boolean belongs is a frame we do not understand, and 'do not understand' is the not-checkable row, never the teardown row.

terminatedReasonRows.name: terminated-phone-restarted-gets-its-own-error
terminatedReasonRows.why: The relay's new reason must reach the user as the true sentence. Falling back to the generic teardown would leave 'Encrypted' on screen with no explanation - the symptom Dennis reported.

terminatedReasonRows.name: terminated-user-left-unchanged
terminatedReasonRows.why: The phone's Disconnect and its 'Doesn't match' refusal both arrive as user_left, and INC-0924's SAS-pending rule owns that copy. This row is the control that proves the new mapping is narrow.

terminatedReasonRows.name: terminated-resume-expired-unchanged
terminatedReasonRows.why: The 180 s expiry. Nothing about it is new and nothing about it should change.

terminatedReasonRows.name: terminated-unknown-future-reason-unchanged
terminatedReasonRows.why: A relay reason this build has never heard of must be a no-op, not a new error string. Otherwise a future relay change silently rewrites this page's copy.
